"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

117:     def _propagate_domains_up(self, hierarchy=("top",)):
118:         from ._xfrm import DomainRenamer
119: 
120:         domain_subfrags = defaultdict(set)
121: 
122:         # For each domain defined by a subfragment, determine which subfragments define it.
123:         for i, (subfrag, name, src_loc) in enumerate(self.subfragments):
124:             # First, recurse into subfragments and let them propagate domains up as well.
125:             hier_name = name
126:             if hier_name is None:
127:                 hier_name = f"<unnamed #{i}>"
128:             subfrag._propagate_domains_up(hierarchy + (hier_name,))
129: 
130:             # Second, classify subfragments by domains they define.
131:             for domain_name, domain in subfrag.domains.items():
132:                 if domain.local:
133:                     continue
134:                 domain_subfrags[domain_name].add((subfrag, name, src_loc, i))
135: 
136:         # For each domain defined by more than one subfragment, rename the domain in each
137:         # of the subfragments such that they no longer conflict.
138:         for domain_name, subfrags in domain_subfrags.items():
139:             if len(subfrags) == 1:
140:                 continue
141: 
142:             names = [n for f, n, s, i in subfrags]
143:             if not all(names):
144:                 names = sorted(f"<unnamed #{i}>" if n is None else f"'{n}'"
145:                                for f, n, s, i in subfrags)
146:                 raise _cd.DomainError(
147:                     "Domain '{}' is defined by subfragments {} of fragment '{}'; it is necessary "
148:                     "to either rename subfragment domains explicitly, or give names to subfragments"
149:                     .format(domain_name, ", ".join(names), ".".join(hierarchy)))
150: 
151:             if len(names) != len(set(names)):
152:                 names = sorted(f"#{i}" for f, n, s, i in subfrags)
153:                 raise _cd.DomainError(
154:                     "Domain '{}' is defined by subfragments {} of fragment '{}', some of which "
155:                     "have identical names; it is necessary to either rename subfragment domains "
156:                     "explicitly, or give distinct names to subfragments"
157:                     .format(domain_name, ", ".join(names), ".".join(hierarchy)))
158: 
159:             for subfrag, name, src_loc, i in subfrags:
160:                 domain_name_map = {domain_name: f"{name}_{domain_name}"}
161:                 self.subfragments[i] = (DomainRenamer(domain_name_map)(subfrag), name, src_loc)
162: 
163:         # Finally, collect the (now unique) subfragment domains, and merge them into our domains.
164:         for i, (subfrag, name, src_loc) in enumerate(self.subfragments):
165:             hier_name = name
166:             if hier_name is None:
167:                 hier_name = f"<unnamed #{i}>"
168:             for domain_name, domain in subfrag.domains.items():
169:                 if domain.local:
170:                     continue
171:                 self.add_domains(domain)
172:                 if domain_name in subfrag.domains_propagated_up:
173:                     _used_in, defined_in = subfrag.domains_propagated_up[domain_name]
174:                 else:
175:                     defined_in = (*hierarchy, hier_name)
176:                 self.domains_propagated_up[domain_name] = (hierarchy, defined_in)
177: 
178:     def _propagate_domains_down(self, hierarchy=("top",)):
179:         # For each domain defined in this fragment, ensure it also exists in all subfragments.
180:         for i, (subfrag, name, src_loc) in enumerate(self.subfragments):
181:             hier_name = name
182:             if hier_name is None:
183:                 hier_name = f"<unnamed #{i}>"
184: 
185:             for domain in self.iter_domains():
186:                 if domain in subfrag.domains:
187:                     assert self.domains[domain] is subfrag.domains[domain]
188:                 else:
189:                     subfrag.add_domains(self.domains[domain])
190:                     if domain in self.domains_propagated_up:
191:                         _used_in, defined_in = self.domains_propagated_up[domain]
192:                         subfrag.domains_propagated_up[domain] = (hierarchy + (hier_name,)), defined_in
193: 
194:             subfrag._propagate_domains_down(hierarchy + (hier_name,))

476:     def _use_signal(self, fragment: Fragment, signal: _ast.Signal):
477:         """Marks a signal as used in a given fragment.
478: 
479:         Also marks a signal as used if it has to be routed through a given fragment to get from
480:         one part of hierarchy to another.  For this purpose, the ``self.signal_lca`` dictionary
481:         is maintained: for every signal, it stores the topmost fragment in which it has been
482:         marked used so far.
483:         """
484:         if signal in self.fragments[fragment].used_signals:
485:             return
486:         self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
487:         if signal not in self.signal_lca:
488:             # First time we see a signal.
489:             self.signal_lca[signal] = fragment
490:             return
491:         # Signal already seen — go from current fragment to the LCA, marking everything along
492:         # the way as used.
493:         lca = self.signal_lca[signal]
494:         # First, go up from our fragment until it is no deeper than current LCA.
495:         while self.fragments[lca].depth < self.fragments[fragment].depth:
496:             fragment = self.fragments[fragment].parent
497:             # Early return if we reach a part of tree where the signal is already marked.
498:             if signal in self.fragments[fragment].used_signals:
499:                 return
500:             self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
501:         # Second, go up from current LCA until it is no deeper than our fragment.
502:         while self.fragments[lca].depth > self.fragments[fragment].depth:
503:             lca = self.fragments[lca].parent
504:             self.fragments[lca].used_signals[signal] = None
505:         # Now, both fragments are at the same depth. Go up from both until the two paths meet.
506:         while fragment is not lca:
507:             lca = self.fragments[lca].parent
508:             self.fragments[lca].used_signals[signal] = None
509:             fragment = self.fragments[fragment].parent
510:             self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
511:         self.signal_lca[signal] = lca
